source_refs.note: Topic 2.7, printed page 34: the definition, the subshell notation and the orbital diagram of boron.

blocks.title: Electronic configuration
blocks.text: Electronic configuration is the distribution of electrons among the available shells, subshells or orbitals of an atom or ion.

For subshells the configuration is written as a list of subshell symbols, one after the other, each with a superscript on the right giving the number of electrons in the subshell. The configuration of a Be-9 atom, with two electrons in the 1s subshell and two in the 2s subshell, is written 1s2 2s2. In an orbital diagram each group of orbitals in a subshell is labelled by its subshell notation and each electron is shown by an arrow, pointing up for s = +1/2 and down for s = -1/2. The orbital diagram of boron (B-11, Z = 5) is 1s with two paired arrows, 2s with two paired arrows, 2px with one arrow, and 2py and 2pz empty.

blocks.alt: Five orbital boxes in a row for boron, labelled 1s, 2s, 2px, 2py and 2pz. 1s and 2s each hold a pair of opposite arrows, 2px holds one arrow, and 2py and 2pz are empty: 1s2 2s2 2px1.
